title: Pointwise invertible simplicial natural transformations give equal homotopy classes
statement: Use small simplicial categories, their path-component categories $\pi_0$, Dwyer--Kan equivalences and the model homotopy category $h\mathrm{sCat}$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property], in fixed containing universes. Let $A,B$ be small simplicial categories and $F,G:A\to B$ simplicial functors. Suppose there is a family of vertex arrows $\eta_a:Fa\to Ga$ such that for every pair $a,a^{\prime}$ the two simplicial maps $A(a,a^{\prime})\to B(Fa,Ga^{\prime})$ given by $u\mapsto\eta_{a^{\prime}}F(u)$ and $u\mapsto G(u)\eta_a$ are equal. Suppose each $[\eta_a]$ is an isomorphism in $\pi_0B$. Then $[F]=[G]$ in $\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(A,B)$. Neither $A$ nor $B$ is required cofibrant or locally Kan; the empty source is allowed.

source.place: Agent-formulated generalization of the natural-transformation step of Lemma A.3.5.6, printed p.894. It follows from Proposition A.3.5.5 and Lemma A.3.5.14, printed pp.893 and 896, by localizing the vertical arrows in [1] times A. It is not claimed to be the literal statement of A.3.4.10. Read online; archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: Let $I=[1]$ be the discrete walking arrow, with distinguished arrow $t:0\to1$, and put $C=I\times A$ using the cartesian product of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-product-parameter]. Define $H:C\to B$ on objects by $H(0,a)=Fa$, $H(1,a)=Ga$. On same-level mapping simplicial sets use $F$ or $G$; on $C((0,a),(1,a^{\prime}))=A(a,a^{\prime})$ use $u\mapsto\eta_{a^{\prime}}F(u)=G(u)\eta_a$; reverse-level mapping sets are empty. These are simplicial maps by the stated enriched naturality. The two mixed composition cases are $H(vu)=\eta_{a^{\prime\prime}}F(v)F(u)=H(v)F(u)$ and $H(vu)=G(v)G(u)\eta_a=G(v)H(u)$. Same-level composition and identities follow from the functor laws. Thus $H$ is an enriched functor. Write $e_0,e_1:A\to C$ for the endpoint inclusions. We have $He_0=F$, $He_1=G$, and $H(t,1_a)=\eta_a$.

proof.text: Use the factorization $I\xrightarrow{j}K\xrightarrow{r}\mathbb J$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-arrow-attachment-localization], with $rj=i:I\to\mathbb J$ and $r$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Apply its localization assertion to $D=I$ with the singleton label represented by $t$, so the attaching functor $I\to D$ is the identity. The defining pushout $\Gamma(I,\{t\})=I\amalg_I K$ is $K$, and its structure map is $j$. Consequently $(K,j)$ is a representative of $(L_{\{t\}}I,q_I)$ under $I$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$. This only specializes the existing node; it does not require a new interval-localization lemma.

source.place: Agent interval-localization argument for the transformation step in HTT Lemma A.3.5.6, printed p.894, using Notation A.3.5.1, Proposition A.3.5.5 and Lemma A.3.5.14, printed pp.891-893 and 896; read online 2026-10-17. Archival HTT WANTED.

proof.text: Cartesian product with $A$ preserves Dwyer--Kan equivalences, in particular $r\times1_A:K\times A\to\mathbb J\times A$. On mapping simplicial sets its maps are products of a weak homotopy equivalence with an identity. The finite-product realization assertion of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] identifies their realizations with products in k-spaces. A path, based sphere map, or based homotopy into a product is exactly a pair of such maps, so path components and all based homotopy groups are products; hence these mapping maps are weak homotopy equivalences. The same path calculation gives $\pi_0(K\times A)=\pi_0K\times\pi_0A$. Taking the product of a quasi-inverse to the given path-component equivalence and its unit and counit with the identity proves equivalence on path-component categories. Thus product with $A$ descends to $h\mathrm{sCat}$, allowing the replacement of $L_{\{t\}}I$ by $K$. Also $p_0:\mathbb J\times A\to A$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence directly: each mapping map is the isomorphism $\{*\}\times A(a,a^{\prime})\to A(a,a^{\prime})$, and every $a$ is the image of $(0,a)$.

proof.text: Put $W_A=\{(t,1_a):a\in\operatorname{Ob}A\}$ and let $q:C\to P=L_{W_A}C$ be localization. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-product-parameter] with first factor $I$, marking $\{t\}$, and second factor $A$, using $(K,j)$ as the localization representative from Step 2. It gives an isomorphism $s:P\to K\times A$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ with $s[q]=[j\times1_A]$. Let $p=[p_0][r\times1_A]s:P\to A$. Both actual functors from Step 3 are Dwyer--Kan equivalences and hence become isomorphisms in the model homotopy category of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]; therefore $p$ is an isomorphism. The relation $rj=i$ gives $p[q]=[p_0(i\times1_A)]=[\operatorname{pr}_A]$. This establishes the projection comparison including its restriction to the original cylinder.

source.place: Agent interval-localization argument for the transformation step in HTT Lemma A.3.5.6, printed p.894, using Notation A.3.5.1, Proposition A.3.5.5 and Lemma A.3.5.14, printed pp.891-893 and 896; read online 2026-10-17. Archival HTT WANTED.

proof.text: By Step 1 the induced path-component functor of $H$ sends every member of $W_A$ to the isomorphism $[\eta_a]$ in $\pi_0B$. The image clause of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property], applied with $C=I\times A$, marking $W_A$ and target $B$, supplies a morphism $h:P\to B$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ with $h[q]=[H]$. Its statement allows the present arbitrary small source and target, so no fibrant or cofibrant replacement is being asserted to preserve strict transformation data.

source.place: Agent interval-localization argument for the transformation step in HTT Lemma A.3.5.6, printed p.894, using Notation A.3.5.1, Proposition A.3.5.5 and Lemma A.3.5.14, printed pp.891-893 and 896; read online 2026-10-17. Archival HTT WANTED.

proof.text: For $k=0,1$, put $u_k=[q][e_k]:A\to P$. Step 4 gives $pu_k=[\operatorname{pr}_A e_k]=1_A$. Since $p$ is invertible, both $u_k$ equal $p^{-1}$, so $u_0=u_1$. Step 5 and the endpoint identities in Step 1 now give $[F]=[H][e_0]=hu_0=hu_1=[H][e_1]=[G]$. For $A=\varnothing$ all the indexing sets and cylinder categories used above are empty; the two endpoint functors are the unique empty functor, and the same identities apply. No step chose strict inverses to the $\eta_a$ or imposed a Kan or cofibrancy hypothesis.

lean.statement: theorem simplicial_natural_equivalence_homotopy (A B : SCat.{u}) (F G : A ⟶ B) (η : ∀ a : underlying A, @Quiver.Hom (underlying B) inferInstance (F.obj a) (G.obj a)) (_hη : ∀ a a' : underlying A, F.map a a' ≫ eHomWhiskerLeft SSet (C := underlying B) (F.obj a) (η a') = G.map a a' ≫ eHomWhiskerRight SSet (C := underlying B) (η a) (G.obj a')) (_hiso : ∀ a : underlying A, IsPiZeroIso (A := underlying B) (η a)) : bergnerHomotopyFunctor.map F = bergnerHomotopyFunctor.map G
lean.note: Enriched naturality is equality of whole mapping simplicial maps, using Mathlib whiskering in the canonical underlying category. IsPiZeroIso tests component invertibility only. No cofibrancy, local Kan, nonemptiness or strict-inverse assumptions.
